terms.comment: No ancient or modern source has a word for the alligator, which the Romans never saw; their crocodīlus is the crocodile of the Nile (Plin. NH 8.89). In everyday talk crocodīlus alone will do.

terms.gloss: one who ties up the vines
terms.comment: A false friend: in Columella, the only author who uses it, the man who ties the vines to their supports. The English word is Spanish el lagarto, ‘the lizard’, from Latin lacerta.

sources: Lewis & Short: crocodilus · Lewis & Short: alligator · Lewis & Short: lacerta
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. American (it has no entry for the alligator, nor have Traupman and Levi–Bini).
